Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Tingling pain in the sole of the right foot upon elevation

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with tingling pain in the sole of the right foot, especially upon elevation and during exercise, with a significant history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and smoking.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello—what brings you in today? Patient: For about six weeks I’ve had a tingling, painful feeling in the sole of my right foot, and it gets worse when I lift my foot above chest level during exercises. With treadmill inclines I also get right calf cramps, and I have to stop and rest often, but the pain completely settles after a few minutes of resting.
Do you have any back pain, or does the pain start in your lower back and radiate down to your leg?

Patient: I don’t have any back pain, and it doesn’t seem to start in my lower back or radiate from there. It’s mainly in the sole of my right foot and shows up with the activity and when I raise that foot.
How old are you, and do you have any history of smoking, diabetes, or high cholesterol?

Patient: I’m 55 years old, I’ve had type 2 diabetes for about 8 years, and I smoke—around two packs a day for roughly 34 years. I don’t know about my cholesterol specifically, but I do have the diabetes and heavy smoking history.
When the pain comes on while walking, does it go away immediately if you simply stop walking and stand still, or do you need to sit down or bend forward to get relief?
Patient: If I stop walking and just stand still, it still eases within a few minutes—I don’t need to sit down or bend forward for it to go away.
Have you noticed any difference in temperature between your right foot and your left foot, or any hair loss, shiny skin, or color changes (like paleness when elevated) on the right leg?

I haven’t noticed a temperature difference between my right and left feet, and I don’t recall any unusual hair loss or shiny skin changes. When I raise the right foot during exercise, it mainly feels like tingling pain, and then it improves after a few minutes of resting.
When you dangle your right foot down (like sitting with it hanging), does the pain improve, and have you noticed if the foot turns more red or purple compared to when you hold it up?

Patient: When I dangle my right foot down, it does tend to improve, and I don’t really notice it turning markedly red or purple compared to the other foot. The main issue is that when I keep it elevated during exercise it gets worse, and it settles after a few minutes of rest.
Does this pain ever wake you up at night, and if so, does hanging your foot off the side of the bed relieve it?

Doctor: Does this pain ever wake you up at night, and if so, does hanging your foot off the side of the bed relieve it? Patient: I haven’t noticed it waking me up at night, and I don’t remember needing to hang my foot off the bed to get relief—it's mainly triggered by activity and when I keep the foot elevated.

[DDX] Peripheral artery disease (intermittent claudication), Lumbar spinal stenosis (neurogenic claudication), Popliteal artery entrapment syndrome, Chronic exertional compartment syndrome, Diabetic peripheral neuropathy
